extracted.intended_audience: Program Directors/Principal Investigators (PDs/PIs) and institutional grant administrators holding eligible NIH research grants who are applying for administrative supplements to promote diversity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for requesting NIH administrative supplements to recruit and support trainees and investigators from underrepresented backgrounds; covers eligibility, allowable activities, application content, review considerations, award administration, and reporting/evaluation metrics. Intended for holders of active NIH parent awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent award active and within scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The parent award must be active and the research proposed in the supplement must be accomplished within the competitive segment and within the original scope of the peer reviewed and approved project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative supplements must support work within the scope of the original project. Any cost increases must result from making modifications to the project that would increase or preserve the overall impact of the project consistent with its originally approved objectives and purposes. At time of supplemental award, the parent award must have support remaining for a reasonable period (usually two years or more).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations administering an eligible parent award may apply for a supplement under this announcement; non-domestic (non-U.S.) entities and non-domestic components of U.S. organizations are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign components (as defined in the NIH Grants Policy Statement) are allowed. Applicants must complete and maintain required registrations (DUNS, SAM, eRA Commons, Grants.gov) prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible activity codes (eligible parent awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative supplements may be requested for many parent award activity codes (extensive list provided: e.g., R01, R21, R03, R15, P01, P30, U01, U54, DP1, DP2, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all participating NIH Institutes and Centers support all listed activity codes; applicants must consult the Table of IC-Specific Information, Requirements and Staff Contacts for details and restrictions (some mechanisms such as P20, P30 eligible only if they contain research components; SC1/SC2/SC3 limited to postdoc and faculty support; policies may vary for R15,R03,R21,R00).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible candidate categories and career-level conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may include high school students, undergraduate students, baccalaureate and master's degree holders, graduate (predoctoral) and health professional students, individuals in postdoctoral training, investigators developing independent research careers, and established investigators who are or become disabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category has specific programmatic purpose and constraints (e.g., baccalaureate/master's: normally 1 year, may be extended; graduate/postdoc: cannot replace existing NRSA/K-related support; investigators developing independent careers: eligibility limited to those without prior independent NIH funding). Appointment of more than one individual to a single award above HS/undergrad depends on parent grant nature and program balance; each request must be strongly justified and include mentoring assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of underrepresented groups (racial/ethnic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals from racial and ethnic groups shown by NSF to be underrepresented in health-related sciences nationally: Blacks/African Americans, Hispanics/Latinos, American Indians/Alaska Natives, Native Hawaiians and other Pacific Islanders. Institutions may also demonstrate local underrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information on racial/ethnic categories and definitions, see OMB Revisions and NSF reports referenced in the FOA. The strength of an institution's description and justification for appointment of an identified candidate will be judged as part of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals with disabilities (diversity category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with disabilities are defined as those with a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities (per Americans with Disabilities Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF data and references are provided. The FOA also allows supplements to established investigators who are or become disabled to request reasonable accommodations (equipment, assistant, modifications) to permit completion of the funded project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds (diversity category and subcriteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disadvantaged background is defined as meeting two or more of seven criteria: (1) were/currently homeless; (2) were/currently in foster care; (3) eligible for Federal Free and Reduced Lunch Program for two+ years; (4) parents/guardians did not complete a bachelor's degree; (5) were/currently eligible for Federal Pell grants; (6) received WIC support as parent/child; (7) grew up in a U.S. rural area or CMS-designated Low-Income & Health Professional Shortage Area (only one of the two in #7 can be used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and definitions are provided in the FOA. Applicants should document how candidates meet these criteria when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women from underrepresented backgrounds (targeting faculty-level diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature shows women from the above backgrounds face particular challenges; NIH encourages institutions to consider women for faculty-level diversity-targeted programs to address recruitment, appointment, retention or advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NSF special reports and NIH references in the FOA. Institutions should justify need based on discipline- or field-specific data when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / immigration eligibility for candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental awards under this announcement are limited to U.S. citizens, non-citizen nationals, or individuals lawfully admitted for permanent residence (Permanent Resident Card, Form I-551).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program may not be used to provide technical support to NIH-supported investigators. Candidates may not receive supplement support if ineligible by citizenship status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions relating to existing federal training support
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals supported by an institutional Kirschstein-NRSA (NRSA) or other PHS funding mechanisms may not be transferred to supplemental support prior to completion of their appointed period of training; supplements are not intended to increase availability of funds to the parent grant for other uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals may be supported by the parent grant short-term pending Institute/Center decision at the recipient's risk. See Pre-Award (Pre-Agreement) Costs in NIH Grants Policy Statement for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term and long-term investigator supplement definitions and effort requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term Investigator Research Supplement: short-term support for faculty to conduct full-time research 3–5 months each year during summer or other academic periods, up to 4 years. Long-term Investigator Research Supplement: support usually for up to two years at a minimum of 9 person months (≈75% effort) during each 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigator must have a doctoral degree, be beyond trainee level, typically junior faculty with at least one year postdoc/equivalent experience. Individuals with prior NIH independent PD/PI funding are not eligible for these supplements. Affiliations with other institutions may be allowed; extraordinary circumstances for working with a former mentor require justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must prepare applications using current forms in accordance with the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide and the eRA Commons Administrative Supplement User Guide. The application forms package must be accessed through ASSIST, Grants.gov Workspace or institutional system-to-system solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All forms must be completed for the supplemental activities only and must not reflect funding or activities for the previously awarded parent award. Conformance to documented requirements is required and strictly enforced. Applications that do not comply may be delayed or not accepted for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget limitations and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Application budgets are limited to no more than the amount of the current parent award and must reflect the actual needs of the proposed project. Direct costs for supplements vary depending on career level (less than $5,000 to more than $100,000). Administrative supplements end with the currently funded competitive cycle of the parent grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests may also be limited by the awarding IC. NIH will prorate funding if the requested budget period is adjusted at the time of award and will use the institution's current F&A rate in effect when new funding is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project period / timing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The project and budget periods for the supplemental award must be within the currently approved project period for the existing parent award (the competitive segment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative supplements end with the currently funded competitive cycle of the parent grant; earliest start dates vary by awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative (not peer) review and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative supplement requests will undergo an administrative evaluation by NIH staff and will not receive full peer review. Applications will be assigned to the awarding component for the parent award and administratively evaluated using the criteria provided in Section V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since only administrative review occurs, NIH policy on resubmission (as for peer-reviewed applications) will not apply. Applicants not accepted for review or not funded should contact the awarding IC before resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Justification/strength of candidate appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength of an institution's description and justification for the appointment of an identified candidate will be judged along with all other aspects of the proposed experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review will consider how the proposed experience will contribute to the candidate's research career development, mentoring assurances, and fit with the parent project's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Human subjects protections (five points)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects and proposed protections, reviewers evaluate: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For exempt research under 45 CFR Part 46, NIH staff will evaluate the justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials. Refer to Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: When projects involve human subjects/NIH-defined clinical research, reviewers will evaluate proposed plans for inclusion or exclusion by sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and age (including children and older adults) to determine if exclusion is scientifically justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should be justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Vertebrate animals (listed points)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH staff will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to points including: (1) description of proposed procedures (species, strains, ages, sex, numbers); (2) justification for use of animals vs alternatives and appropriateness of species; (3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain and injury; and (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH staff will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to personnel and/or the environment, and whether adequate protections are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must describe biosafety protections and institutional capabilities to manage hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of applications per parent award and multiple appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: A parent award may support more than one individual on a supplement, but each request must be strongly justified and include assurances that each candidate will receive appropriate mentoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are encouraged to recruit more than one high school or undergraduate student. Appointment of more than one individual above HS/undergrad depends on parent grant nature and program balance. Candidates may receive support from only one administrative supplement at a time, but may be supported by more than one supplement during career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must have required registrations in place prior to submission: DUNS number, System for Award Management (SAM), eRA Commons, and Grants.gov (if submitting via Grants.gov). PD/PI must have an eRA Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations can take many weeks; failure to complete registrations in advance is not an acceptable reason for late submission. The same DUNS must be used for all registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: This FOA is designed specifically for applicants proposing research that does not involve leading an independent clinical trial, a clinical trial feasibility study, or an ancillary clinical trial. Applicants may propose research experience in a clinical trial led by a mentor or co-mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants are unsure whether their work constitutes a clinical trial, they should seek help (FOA references NIH guidance on clinical trial determination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and progress evaluation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reporting for supplements must be included and clearly delineated from the parent award in non-competing continuation applications and submitted via the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR). NIH may request information for program evaluation post-award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation of supplement support depends on satisfactory review of progress for both the parent award and the supplement. Awardees must comply with reporting (including FSRS reporting for subawards over $25,000 where applicable) and FAPIIS integrity/performance disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will evaluate the program within ten years using measures such as aggregate number and demographics of participants and subsequent educational/career progress (degree completion, enrollment in advanced programs, participation in research, employment in research fields, authorship, and independent grant support) for undergraduate, graduate, postdoctorate, and early career participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may contact participants after award completion for updates on employment, publications, support, honors, and other outcomes to assess program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with NIH and federal policies and legal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are subject to the NIH Grants Policy Statement, HHS and federal civil rights laws (nondiscrimination, accessibility for persons with limited English proficiency, obligations for serving persons with disabilities), sexual harassment policies, conscience/religious discrimination laws, and other applicable statutes/regulations (e.g., FAPIIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees must ensure programs comply with these legal obligations and NIH policy notices; contact NIH Office for Civil Rights or Scientific/Research Contact for guidance when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: This FOA does not require cost sharing as defined in the NIH Grants Policy Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget submissions should reflect actual needs and conform to awarding IC limitations; cost sharing not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special eligibility: reasonable accommodations for disabled PD(s)/PI(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators on NIH research, program project, or center grants who are or become disabled during the current project period may request funds for reasonable accommodations (special equipment, assistant, or other modifications) to permit completion of the currently funded research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be justified and related to enabling continued work on the funded project within its scope.
